page: Microsoft Azure GS4-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the GS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, with a thread-per-core ratio of 1.0. It is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core density of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 459 GB, and there are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark data reveals significant performance tradeoffs, particularly regarding compute speed and memory write bandwidth. Single-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance is also relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 454.13 GB/sec, large-block memory write bandwidth is poor, ranking in the bottom 10% at 13.09 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates average capabilities in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations, which reached 6.85 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the GS4-8 offers a high resource density of memory relative to its compute footprint, making it a specialized option where RAM capacity is prioritized over raw CPU speed. Given these characteristics, the instance is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-thread performance. Appropriate workloads include database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing tasks that can leverage the 224.0 GB RAM allocation and local 459 GB storage.
